name: Slip trailing
summary: Liquid clay, called slip, is trailed from a quill or a pipe onto the leather-hard pot in lines and dots. The lines stay raised under the glaze.
how: Mix slip to the thickness of cream.
Fill a pipe or a bag with the slip.
Draw lines 2 to 4 mm wide on a pot in a contrast colour.
Dip the pot in clear lead glaze and fire it at about 1050 °C.

origin.note: Thomas Toft and other Staffordshire potters trail slip pictures on large dishes.

adoptions.via: Staffordshire potters trail cream slip pictures and names on red earthenware dishes.
